about: Measured facts about how this band model renders UI, tied to one firmware version (`firmware`). Every leaf is {value, status, source, date}: status "measured" (from a device photo or observation), "assumed" (from a spec, a font file or another model) or "unknown" (value null). Top level: `device` and `screen` (the panel itself, true for everything drawn on it). `quickapp`: how the Vela quick-app (JS app) renderer draws text, boxes, CSS, colour, images and animation. `face`: how the watch-face engine (band10-toolkit .bin faces: widgets, image lists, the Lua layer, always-on) draws; a different renderer, so quick-app facts never stand in for face facts. Layout code reads it through tools/vela-calib/profile.js (quick-app paths like 'font.line_box_em' resolve inside `quickapp`); tools/vela-calib/measure.py writes it from photos of the calibration app. Units: band px (= design px when designWidth = the screen width; the geometry page checks it) and em (x font-size).

firmware.note: Every measured fact here was measured on this firmware. After a firmware update, re-run the calibration kit (tools/vela-calib) and compare before trusting the profile; then bump this.

firmware.source: Mi Fitness device page of a Band 11

design_width.note: manifest designWidth 212 draws 1 design px per panel px: the end arcs fit radius {'top': 103.32, 'bottom': 103.44} centred at x [105.67, 105.92]

design_scale.note: W/2 over the fitted end radius: ~1.00-1.03 when 1 design px = 1 panel px (a capsule end radius is half the panel width)

corner_radius_px.note: capsule: each end is one arc; given per corner so profile.js safeArea / xRange work unchanged

left.note: from the outer ends of the ruler ticks (bloom-corrected), +-1 px; the Screen geometry page measures it directly

right.note: from the outer ends of the ruler ticks (bloom-corrected), +-1 px; the Screen geometry page measures it directly

system_overlay.source: Vela Calib 2.0.0 Screen geometry page: observe (measure.py set)

end_radius_px.note: radius of each semicircular end (bloom-corrected), band px

family.source: a Text W / Text V photo compared with the font files

digit.note: round digits, from the line-box top, half-brightness edges (includes ~1 px camera bloom per side, so slightly large = conservative)

assumed.source: kit policy (profile.js width() safety), copied from band10pro; not a device fact
assumed.note: 2026-09-27 photos: every measured bold string is 0.79-1.07x the assumed table (letters 0.92-1.00, digits 0.79 ('1') to 1.03, '0 0 0 0' 1.07 because the space is 0.339 em, not 0.283). 1.1 still covers all of them. Digit strings run about 1 px per glyph wider than the table's em widths (0000: 65.0/127.7/250.2 px at 24/48/96 = 0.64 em + 1 px per glyph), so at small sizes the fixed px matters: at 16 px a digit string reaches ~1.10x.

measured.source: kit policy (profile.js width() safety), copied from band10pro; not a device fact
measured.note: Widths measured at one size carry ~1 px per glyph of fixed tracking: a digit advance measured at 48 px (em + 1/48) under-reads at 24 px by ~0.02 em per glyph (3 %), over-reads at larger sizes. 1.02 covers sizes >= ~30 px; below that add 1 px per glyph.

Written by tools/face-calib/measure_face.py (this key only). Quick-app facts never stand in for these.

api_status.note: ok = the pcall returned; error = it raised; not_drawn = the script never got there (or did not run)

placement_offset_px.note: drawn position minus the requested x, y (band px, +-0.5)

align.note: anchor_* = x is the left/centre/right of the digits drawn; box_* = the digits are aligned inside a slot of `count` cells starting at x. Only told apart when fewer digits than `count` are drawn.

spacing_px.note: requested spacing -> measured gap between cells; a huge gap for -3 means the byte is read unsigned

unit_gap_px.note: gap between the last digit and the unit image

fallback.note: several names = this battery value cannot tell them apart; retake at another charge

u16_values.note: frame shown for steps with frames at 0/1000/5000/10000 (values above 255 work if not always 0)

image_list_frames_same_size.status_note: format rule: an image-list block has one width/height for all frames (parser/imageCodec.ts)
